Few areas of the Internet are evolving as quickly as consumer AI. User growth is still running at an extraordinary pace, new products and features are launching seemingly every week, and market positions continue to shift as platforms compete for users’ attention. But the underlying question remains the same: what are consumers actually using? In this recurring tracker, we monitor the key app and web metrics across major AI platforms to help investors follow adoption trends, gauge competitive momentum, and identify the winners and losers as the category matures.
ChatGPT remains the clear leader in consumer AI, maintaining a dominant position across downloads, MAU, and DAU globally and in the US. The platform still accounts for \~64% of global AI app MAUs and \~60% in the US, while its lead is even larger on DAU given its superior engagement. ChatGPT continues to post the highest DAU/MAU ratios (\~40-45%) and 7-day retention rates (\~25-30%) among major chatbot platforms, suggesting users engage with the product more frequently and more consistently than competitors. Gemini has established itself as the clear No. 2 player globally, while the US market remains more competitive, with Claude continuing to gain traction and narrowing the gap on several user metrics.
The Agents are coming... ChatGPT still leads app downloads by a wide margin, but download growth has slowed materially, turning negative Y/Y since April 2026 in both global and US markets. By contrast, Gemini, Claude, and Meta AI/Muse are growing rapidly off smaller bases. Between August 2025 and August 2026, ChatGPT's global MAU share declined from 78% to 64%, while Gemini increased its share from 19% to 26%. The trend is even more pronounced in the US, where ChatGPT's MAU share declined from 79% to 60% in the past 1 year, while Gemini increased its share from 13% to 19% and Claude grew from 2% to 9%. Recently the success of Meta’s Muse rising to the top of the app charts and dominating the news cycle may usher in the next wave of consumer AI agent apps in the months ahead. While too early, we await retention and engagement metrics on Muse.
Engagement metrics maturing for the category. Across most leading chatbot apps, user behavior has converged around 14-17 minutes of daily usage, 8-9 sessions per day, and roughly 1.5-2 minute session lengths, suggesting AI chatbots are becoming a habitual consumer product. ChatGPT remains the most engaged platform, leading in both DAU/MAU ratio and retention rate. The new Meta Muse agent is showing encouraging early momentum, which could be a catalyst to deepen engagement in the sector.
GenAI is rapidly emerging as a new commerce search-and-discovery channel, but AI traffic is growing quickly off a small base. AI referrals still account for <1.5% of overall web traffic to eCommerce and retail websites, suggesting AI-driven commerce remains in its early stages. There are some signs that AI is beginning to influence consumer discovery and traffic patterns across industries. Booking has acknowledged that AI is affecting parts of its search-driven discovery funnel, while Reddit's CEO has noted that Google AI Overviews have not been a meaningful source of traffic, raising concerns that AIgenerated answers may reduce referrals to open-web destinations. Similar dynamics are beginning to emerge in other sectors (e.g. pest control). Meta’s Muse and the new Siri will be key products to watch on this front.

DETAILS
RECENT KEY UPDATES
The consumer AI landscape continues to evolve rapidly, with major platforms simultaneously scaling users, releasing new models, and expanding product capabilities. While ChatGPT, Gemini, Meta AI, Claude, Grok, and Alexa+ are all benefiting from growing consumer adoption of AI, each is pursuing a distinct strategy, ranging from standalone AI assistants to AI embedded within search, social, messaging, and commerce ecosystems.
ChatGPT remains the leading standalone AI application, surpassing 1 billion weekly active users. Management has increasingly emphasized ChatGPT becoming a daily-use product across writing, research, coding, learning, and productivity workflows. OpenAI also recently disclosed that its advertising business has reached an approximately \$1B annual revenue run rate.
• Google reported that the Gemini app surpassed 1B MAUs, while AI Mode exceeded 1 billion users and AI Overviews reached >2.5 billion monthly users, underscoring the company's unparalleled distribution advantage. Beyond the standalone Gemini app, Google continues to integrate AI experiences across Search, Maps, Gmail, Android, and other consumer products, while expanding AI Mode and AI Overviews with more conversational search, deeper followup questions, and shopping capabilities. Looking ahead, investors are increasingly focused on Google's next major frontier-model release, as the company has not introduced a significant flagship-model upgrade for some time relative to the faster release cadence at OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.
Meta AI surpassed 1 billion monthly active users, making it one of the largest AI assistants globally. Meta continues to expand Meta AI across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and Messenger, with management increasingly emphasizing engagement within its existing apps rather than through the standalone Meta AI app, leveraging the company's massive user base and distribution advantage. The company has also continued advancing its AI capabilities through the Muse family, introducing new agentic, multimodal, and voice capabilities, including Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Voice Transcribe.
• Meta also launched Muse on September 8, 2026, a standalone consumer AI agent designed to help users complete tasks, and it already climbed to #1 on the U.S. App Store, with impressive early download volume benchmarked against ChatGPT and Meta AI.
Amazon's most important consumer AI initiative remains Alexa+, its next-generation AI assistant being rolled out across Echo devices, Fire TV, and Amazon's broader smart-home platform. With an installed base of over 600 million devices, Amazon has one of the largest consumer AI distribution networks globally. Recent disclosures point to strong early adoption, with >350 million customers used Alexa in the last 12 months, engagement accelerated in 2Q and interactions up 5x Y/Y. Alexa+ users are engaging 2-3x more frequently, increasing smart-home engagement by nearly 50% in the first month, and interacting with Alexa-integrated services 6x more. As Alexa+ evolves from a voice assistant into an agent capable of discovering, booking, and purchasing products and services, we continue to believe Amazon is well positioned for an eventual agentic commerce opportunity given its unique combination of shopping intent, payments, fulfillment, and distribution.
Anthropic continued to advance Claude's capabilities through the rollout of its Claude 5 model family, including frontier model Fable 5 and the launch of Claude Opus 5 in July 2026, which delivers near-frontier performance on reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks at lower cost. The company also continued expanding Claude's productivity and task-execution capabilities, further positioning the platform as a productivity-focused AI assistant capable of handling increasingly complex workflows.
CONSUMER AI CHATBOT ADOPTION
• Downloads: ChatGPT still leads, but its growth is slowing down while competitors still remain high
ChatGPT continues to lead global downloads by a wide margin, with Gemini remaining the clear No. 2. ChatGPT also leads in US downloads, while competition for the No. 2 spot remains intense among Claude, Gemini, and Meta AI. We do note that Gemini is pre-installed on some Android devices, likely making its download share lower than its newly activated user share.

Looking at global download growth, ChatGPT has been negative year over year since April 2026 and declined 27% YoY in August. In contrast, Gemini, Claude and Meta AI continued to post strong growth in August (+79%, +754%, and +363%, respectively). Combined downloads across the five chatbots we track were +6% YoY in August, signaling early signs of plateauing.
A similar trend is seen in the US. ChatGPT's downloads have been negative YoY since April 2026 and were down 9% in August. Meanwhile, Gemini, Claude, and Meta AI continued to deliver positive growth (+29%, +421%, and +471%, respectively). Combined downloads across the five chatbots we track grew 18% YoY in August.
• MAU: ChatGPT remains the scale leader, while competitors are growing faster off smaller bases
• ChatGPT continues to dominate global MAU, with Gemini remaining the clear No. 2.
• In the US, ChatGPT remains the market leader, although had a dip in spring when Claude gained meaningful share. Gemini remains firmly in second place, while Claude has seen the fastest recent growth.
• Global MAU growth remains robust, led by emerging challengers. August MAU grew 70% YoY for ChatGPT, 190% for Gemini, 1228% for Claude, and 704% for Meta AI. Combined MAU across the five chatbot apps we track rose 108% YoY.
• In the US, ChatGPT's growth continue to be strong at 49% YoY in August, while Gemini, Claude, and Meta AI continued to grow rapidly at 185%, 1031%, and 611%, respectively. Combined MAU across the five apps increased 95% YoY.
• Incremental users captured: Gemini/Claude/Meta AI are capturing a disproportionate share of industry growth.
Globally, ChatGPT's MAU share declined from 78% to 64% between Aug. 2025 and Aug. 2026, but it still accounted for \~55% of incremental MAU growth in May-Aug. 2026. Gemini was the biggest share gainer, capturing 36% of incremental MAU in May-Aug. 2026, and its MAU share increased from 19% to 26% in the past \~1 year. Claude captured \~12% of incremental MAU in recent 3 months.
• The shift has been even more pronounced in the US, where ChatGPT's share fell from 79% to 60% in the past year, and it captured only \~44% of incremental MAU growth in May-Aug. 2026. Gemini captured 32% of incremental MAU in the past 3 months, raising its MAU share from 13% to 19% in the past 1 year, while Claude captured 18% of incremental MAU in the past 3 months and grew to a 9% MAU share.

THE CONSUMER AI AGENTIC INFLECTION? WELCOME TO THE PARTY META MUSE
Meta launched Muse on September 8, 2026, introducing a standalone consumer AI agent designed to move beyond traditional chat interfaces and help users complete tasks on their behalf. Within 10 days of launch, Muse climbed to #1 on the U.S. App Store, overtaking ChatGPT on September 17, highlighting strong early consumer interest. If we look at downloads number after release date, Muse is already trending higher than when the ChatGPT app was released on May 18th 2023.
The strong early adoption is supported by significant distribution advantages through Meta's family of apps, including in-app promotion across Instagram, Facebook, Threads, etc. Growth also appears to be aided by referral incentives that provide users with additional usage credits/tokens for inviting friends.
Positive early feedback has been encouraging:
• Based on our consumer checks, users think Muse’s interface feels more conversational and human than many competing assistants, leveraging avatars, emojis, and a more personalized design.
Our initial testing suggests Muse can perform a range of everyday consumer tasks reasonably well, including booking doctor appointments, setting reminders and personal goals, monitoring flight prices, contacting customer service, and canceling subscriptions, etc. It seems that Muse's ability to complete real-world tasks rather than simply generate answers is evident, suggesting Meta may be making progress toward broader consumer adoption of agentic AI.
Muse's integration with Instagram and Threads provides access to social context that can be particularly useful for trip planning, local discovery, and restaurant recommendations. In addition, some consumers may view privacy concerns as less incremental versus competing agents given Meta already possesses extensive first-party user data.
That said, early limitations remain apparent:
• Performance has been inconsistent in some seemingly straightforward agentic use cases, including hotel room reservations, where reliability can vary.
Privacy also remains a debate among consumers: while broader permissions enable more powerful agent capabilities, some users are reluctant to grant deep access given ongoing concerns around Meta's data collection and privacy practices. As a result, users who restrict permissions may experience a materially narrower set of functionalities.

Consumers may not want another AI assistant. Users who already rely on ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini may prefer to consolidate usage within a single primary assistant, particularly if competing products can perform many of the same tasks. This underscores the importance of Meta's unique social graph and ecosystem advantages as key differentiators.
Early traction is encouraging, but we need KPIs that show sustained engagement. We see meaningful long-term potential in the platform and view its early download momentum as encouraging, although it remains too early to assess whether engagement and adoption levels will prove sustainable.
In consumer internet, attention is the currency. Trying an AI assistant once is very different from relying on it every day. Investor focus is likely to shift from headline user growth to evidence of sustained engagement: 7 and 28 day retention rates, continued expansion of the WAU/MAU base and, increasingly, DAUs as a measure of daily utility. Metrics such as DAU/WAU and DAU/MAU will become critical indicators of whether Muse is becoming part of users' routines rather than just another app they occasionally visit.
Meta is subsidizing usage today to learn behavior and drive adoption. Meta is currently monetizing Muse through a tiered subscription model. Users receive access to a free plan that includes up to 100M tokens per week, which is a VERY decent amount of tokens to experiment with for most everyday agent tasks. For heavier users, Meta offers a Power tier at \$20/month with 500M tokens per week, and a Maximum tier at \$100/month with 3B tokens per week.
• In practice, we expect most users today to remain on the free plan as they experiment with the product and discover potential use cases. As a result, Muse's near-term monetization opportunity is likely limited, with Meta prioritizing adoption, engagement, and product iteration over revenue maximization. The current pricing structure suggests Meta is willing to absorb a significant portion of inference costs in exchange for user growth and learning, with subscriptions providing an early framework for monetization as power-user demand emerges.
And narratives change fast in this market. We expect every major AI platform to continue investing, creating a steady stream of product launches, partnerships, and announcements. As a result, watch out….for today's PR excitement for Muse can quickly rotate as new entrants capture attention and reshape the narrative.
• Instinct has taken Silicon Valley by storm. What began as a limited rollout earlier this year has quickly scaled to more than 100,000 users, with demand fast outpacing available compute capacity.
• Where's Google? Right here, just making less noise. While startups and AI challengers dominate the headlines, Google has quietly built a very compelling agentic AI offering in the market. At the center of this push isGemini Spark, a 24/7 personal AI agent designed to move Gemini from simply answering questions to actively getting work done on a user's behalf. Spark can monitor inboxes, summarize updates, create workflows across Gmail, Docs and other Workspace applications, generate reports from meeting notes, and proactively manage recurring tasks, all while continuing to operate in the background even when a user's device is offline. Google's new Daily Brief feature further strengthens its vision of a proactive assistant by delivering personalized updates and recommended actions based on information from connected apps. Together, these capabilities give Google many of the building blocks of a true personal AI agent. With more aggressive marketing, broader developer integrations, and deeper ecosystem activation, Google has an opportunity to turn Gemini's quiet progress into meaningful mind share leadership.
Where’s OpenAI? We expect an updated consumer agent offering coming soon with reports that the company is also working on its own personal AI assistant.
